title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 21 Aug 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.86 km2 to 30.63 km2 over 48 days. HV fell slightly and HH rose slightly across the land.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by -1.23 km2, or -3.9%. Mean HV moved by -0.16 dB and mean HH by 0.34 dB. In HH, 1.85 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.26 km2 darker; in HV, 0.49 km2 turned brighter and 0.38 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 0.76 km2 brighter in HH and rose 0.46 dB. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes fell by 0.18 dB in HV. The changing fields type rose 0.83 dB in HV. Built-up land rose 0.5 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's records would confirm it. Possible cause for lower HV on the slopes: shrub and grass drying in the hot season; the optical photo would show how green they are. Possible cause for higher HH, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the dates.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 12.7% and 10.4% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 1.23 km2 loss with the dam's level change. Treat HH shifts of a few tenths of a dB as uncertain until stable targets confirm them.
